กำแพงจวนเจ้าเมืองตะกั่วป่าน่าจะสร้างขึ้น: The Takua Pa Governor's Residence Wall was probably built during the tenure of Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch Na Nakhon), governor of Takua Pa, between 1840 and 1881 (B.E. 2383 to 2424), but academic sources have not established a definite construction year. The wall enclosed the residence and administrative area, serving much like a fortification to protect against danger and provide shelter for townspeople.
หลังพระยาเสนานุชิต (นุช) พ้นตำแหน่ง กำแพ: After Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch) left office, the wall and residence continued to be used during the tenure of Phraya Senanuchit (Iam Na Nakhon), from 1881 to 1892 (B.E. 2424 to 2435). King Chulalongkorn visited Takua Pa and viewed the residence on 28 May, R.S. 109, or 1890 (B.E. 2433).
พื้นที่ไม่ได้ทำหน้าที่เป็นที่พักของเจ้าเ: The site no longer serves as the governor's residence, but remains a landmark in the old town and a venue for ceremonies and community activities. In 2026 (B.E. 2569), Phang Nga Province and Takua Pa Municipality held the event "From Takola to Takua Pa, 12th edition" at the residence from 28 February to 3 March, with performances of khon, Nora and nang talung, religious ceremonies and Buddhist chanting, as well as local food and OTOP products for sale.
The site's archaeological period is estimated at 1840 to 1881 (B.E. 2383 to 2424). It is thought to have been built during the tenure of Phraya Senanuchit (Nuch Na Nakhon), governor of Takua Pa, as a wall around the residence and a defense against enemies.

พ.ศ. 2511 มีการนำเหล็กจากเรือขุดแร่มาสร้: In 1968 (B.E. 2511), steel from a mining dredger was used to build the Khok Khanun Iron Bridge, more than 200 metres long, across the Takua Pa River. The initiative came from Juti Boonsung, owner of Juti Boonsung Mining Dredger Co., Ltd., founded in 1960 (B.E. 2503).

ตึกแถวเลขที่ 53 ถนนราษฎร์บำรุง ย่านตลาดเ: Shophouse No. 53 on Thanon Rat Bamrung in the old market district is a teak house that now operates as a cafe, making it one of the few buildings on this street that visitors can enter and see inside.
ข้อมูลทะเบียนตลาดของกรมการค้าภายในระบุว่: The Department of Internal Trade's market registration records state that Takua Pa Old Town Cultural Street is on Thanon Si Takua Pa and Thanon Udom Thara. It opens on Sundays from 14:00 to 20:00, with free entry to the activities. The records identify an operator at the market-system level but do not identify a separate legal entity responsible for the street.
หลักฐานล่าสุดที่พบยืนยันการมีอยู่ของตลาด: The latest evidence found confirms that Lan Loeng Market existed during 2024 to 2025 (B.E. 2567 to 2568) and indicates that small vendors were still using the area to sell food. The municipality previously gave approximate opening hours of 08:00 to 22:00, but review platforms list a different schedule, so the current hours should not be treated as verified.
